## From pressure to specialization {#motivation-route}

This section explains why [modern compiler techniques]{.marker} must reach into hardware.

::: {.incremental}
1. **Layers:** follow arithmetic choices from programs toward circuits.

2. **Scaling limits:** understand why performance no longer arrives for free.

3. **Specialization:** connect GPUs, TPUs, and new number formats.
:::

## Arithmetic optimization spans the stack {#motivation-hardware-freedom}

::::: {.column width="52%"}

::::: {.column width="48%"}
:::: {.r-stack .motivation-layer-copy}
::: {.motivation-layer-copy-state .fragment .fade-out .instant-fragment data-fragment-index="0"}
[One problem, many representations]{.motivation-state-label}

- Each layer exposes different decisions.

- Software and hardware are intertwined and **multi-level**.
:::

::: {.motivation-layer-copy-state .fragment .fade-in-then-out .instant-fragment data-fragment-index="0"}
[1. Optimize a fixed machine]{.motivation-state-label}

- Algebraic simplification: $x \times 1 \rightarrow x$.

- Strength reduction: $x \times 2 \rightarrow x \ll 1$.

- Instruction selection: fused multiply-add.

**A compiler usually sees a local window.**
:::

::: {.motivation-layer-copy-state .fragment .fade-in-then-out .instant-fragment data-fragment-index="1"}
[2. Build the machine]{.motivation-state-label}

- High-level synthesis crosses the ISA boundary.

- Specialize operators: $x^2$, $x/3$.

- Fuse operators and map them to LUTs or DSPs.

**More hardware freedom means more opportunities.**
:::

::: {.motivation-layer-copy-state .fragment .fade-in-then-out .instant-fragment data-fragment-index="2"}
[3. Traverse the stack]{.motivation-state-label}

- MLIR dialects keep domain intent explicit.

- Lowerings connect many domain-specific representations.

- One infrastructure can move from problem to circuit.

**MLIR offers a larger view.**
:::

::: {.motivation-layer-copy-state .fragment .instant-fragment data-fragment-index="3"}
[This presentation lives here!]{.motivation-state-label .motivation-state-label-impact .marker}

- **Logic / RTL:** hardware structure, datapaths, and state.

- **Circuits:** Boolean networks, synthesis, and cost.

- **Hands-on:** lower arithmetic operations into explicit circuits.
:::
::::
:::::
::::::

## Promotion time! {#motivation-team-arithmetic}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%"}
![*Application-Specific Arithmetic*, de Dinechin and Kumm, 2024. [@dinechin2024asa]](assets/images/motivation/application-specific-arithmetic-cover-hires.jpg){fig-align="center" fig-alt="Cover of Application-Specific Arithmetic by Florent de Dinechin and Martin Kumm" height="520"}
:::

::: {.column width="66%"}
**Today's bias:** we will look at hardware through **arithmetic** and **small
floating-point formats**.

::: {.incremental}
- **Emeraude:** make number formats and operators part of the design space.

- **FloPoCo:** generate arithmetic operators for a target, a frequency, and a
  numerical contract.

- **Hands-on:** build an E4M3 multiplier; if time permits, specialize its
  datapath into a squarer.
:::
:::
